Identify the main sources of water such as rain, oceans, rivers, springs, wells, ponds, and reservoirs.

Explain the difference between fresh water and salt water.

Differentiate between ponds and reservoirs by their size, water storage capacity, and uses.
Appreciate the role of water in daily life and list various uses of water at home and school.
Understand the physical properties of water such as being colorless, odorless, and tasteless.
Perform simple activities to observe the physical characteristics of water and verify related facts.
Understand the biological importance of water in the growth of plants and the survival of animals.
Recognize cultural and traditional practices related to water conservation and worship in their community.
Identify causes and effects of water pollution, including physical, chemical, and biological pollution.
Understand the health hazards caused by contaminated water such as cholera, diarrhea, and malaria.
Learn preventive measures to maintain potable (pure) water and promote good health.
